techniques.name: Reciprocity
techniques.bounds: Offer real upfront value such as a checklist, template, or audit insight before asking for a higher-friction action.

techniques.name: Commitment and consistency
techniques.bounds: Ask for a small honest next step; do not hide costs or escalate commitments without clarity.

techniques.name: Social proof
techniques.bounds: Use only verified customer counts, reviews, testimonials, or behavior; fake reviews and invented popularity are out of bounds.

techniques.name: Authority
techniques.bounds: Name the real credential, source, benchmark, or audit evidence; vague expert claims are insufficient.

techniques.name: Loss aversion
techniques.bounds: Frame only real time, money, risk, or opportunity costs supported by service-profile evidence; fearmongering is out of bounds.

techniques.name: Anchoring
techniques.bounds: Use truthful prices, benchmarks, time savings, or current-alternative costs; fabricated list prices and arbitrary ROI are out of bounds.

techniques.name: Scarcity and FOMO
techniques.bounds: Only real capacity, cohort, deadline, inventory, or beta-access limits may be used; false urgency and fake countdowns are out of bounds.

techniques.name: Copy structure: AIDA, PAS, FAB
techniques.bounds: Use formulas as structure, not as proof of performance; keep pain agitation truthful and proportional.

techniques.name: Value proposition fit
techniques.bounds: Map jobs, pains, and gains from the service profile to explicit pain relievers and gain creators.

techniques.name: Lifecycle next action
techniques.bounds: Each email should ask for one behavior-based next action and suppress messages that no longer match the user's state.
